Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa | National 700 participants at GABS 2026 signal growing German interest in Africa – Dr Michael Blank Source : Albert Kuzor 25 November 2026 3:01pm The Delegate of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana, Dr Michael Blank. ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
About 700 participants at the 2026 German-African Business Summit (GABS) in Accra demonstrate growing interest among German companies in investment opportunities across Africa, the Delegate of German Industry and Commerce in Ghana, Dr Michael Blank, has said.
He said the strong participation at the summit reflects increasing attention from German businesses towards the continent, particularly Ghana.
In an interview with JoyBusiness on the sidelines of the summit, Dr Blank said the event came at a crucial point in Ghanaian-German business relations.
"We are really happy that it's now coming to Ghana back again. Why? Because we are at a crucial point in Ghanaian-German business relationships," he said.
He added that the growing interest was evident in the number of participants who travelled to Ghana for the event.
"You can tell from the impact and the amount of people who came to Ghana. We had about 700 visitors, which is actually quite a lot," he noted.
Dr Blank said the summit also provided an opportunity to assess changing attitudes towards international business partnerships, observing that African countries were becoming increasingly confident in choosing their investment partners.
He said Germany could strengthen its position as a preferred partner if its companies adapted to the needs and priorities of African countries.
Among the areas he identified were supporting local production to reduce imports and investing in education and skills training.
"Another thing is maybe not only to produce here, but also to educate people and to train people. So these two things, if you combine it, can really make a difference," he said.
